clue.text: Part of the mass is intoned in Franciscan setting

indicators.note: Part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A church service in which part of the Mass is chanted, set somewhere Franciscan.
explanation.walkthrough: The run sits across 'mass is intoned'. The Italian hill town where St Francis was born and founded his order is the setting.
explanation.definitionFit: The Umbrian town is the birthplace of St Francis and home of his basilica, so it is the Franciscan order's home ground.

clue.text: Sir Anthony is unqualified

explanation.definitionFit: Sir Anthony is the tyrannical father in Sheridan's comedy The Rivals; the surname also means complete and unconditional.

clue.text: Fruit drink her best order?

indicators.note: putting in order means arranging, so these letters are sorted afresh

explanation.surface: Asking for her favourite fruit cordial at a bar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'order' looks like a request at the bar; it rearranges HERBEST.
explanation.definitionFit: A sherbet was originally a cooling Middle Eastern drink of sweetened fruit juice.

clue.text: Several dates are off and on

parts.note: several means some
dates are times

explanation.surface: Several appointments are cancelled and then revived.
explanation.definitionFit: Occasionally, now and then, rather than all the time.

clue.text: Lead soldiers?

parts.note: reads like toy figures cast in metal, but means the troops who go in front of an army

explanation.walkthrough: 'Lead' looks like the metal of toy soldiers; it is the verb sense, troops at the head of an advance.
explanation.definitionFit: The foremost division of an advancing army is its front line, the troops leading the way.

clue.text: Recommended discipline in community home

parts.note: something recommended has been approved
a school is a branch of learning or discipline

explanation.surface: Suggested punishment in a care home.
explanation.walkthrough: Approved schools were British residential institutions for young offenders, renamed community homes in the 1970s.
explanation.definitionFit: The old British reform institution for delinquent youngsters was replaced by local authority care units.

clue.text: Spirit produced by light rubber?

parts.note: the rubber is not a thin eraser but a person rubbing a lamp, as Aladdin did to summon a magic being

explanation.walkthrough: 'light rubber' suggests a thin eraser; it is someone rubbing a light, Aladdin's lamp.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Arabian Nights a magical being, a jinn, appears when the lamp is rubbed.

clue.text: Accountant, it is said in France, invested in gold

indicators.note: invested in means put inside, like money placed in a fund

parts.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold
or is gold in heraldry and in French
dit is French for said

explanation.surface: Gossip in France that an accountant has put money into gold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gold' supplies both its symbol AU and the heraldic OR, and DIT goes between them.
explanation.definitionFit: An auditor is a person who checks the books, a kind of accountant.

clue.text: Superior light unit trapped in river

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Scotland, Wales and England
the lux is the SI unit of illumination

explanation.surface: A high-end lamp fitting caught in a river.
explanation.definitionFit: A de luxe product is luxurious, of a higher grade than standard.

clue.text: Typical daily deed involving argument

parts.note: a daily is a British cleaning woman, also called a char
a deed is an act
eristic is the art of disputation or argument

explanation.surface: An everyday act that involves a quarrel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'daily' looks like 'every day' or a newspaper; in Britain a daily or char is a cleaner who comes in each day.
explanation.definitionFit: Something distinctive of a person or thing is typical of them.

clue.text: Subject of mishap set at sea?

definitions.text: Subject of mishap set at sea?

indicators.note: at sea means confused or all over the place, so the letters of these two words are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: Something that might suffer an accident while sailing the ocean.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at sea' rearranges MISHAPSET; the whole clue doubles as a description of a vessel that could meet disaster on the ocean.
explanation.definitionFit: A powered ocean-going vessel is just the kind of craft that suffers a mishap on the open sea.

clue.text: Like a lump, having no pulse

parts.note: taken as written
dal is a pulse, the split lentils or peas of Indian cooking

explanation.surface: Something lumpy that has no heartbeat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pulse' suggests a heartbeat, but it is the edible seed, dal.
explanation.definitionFit: A node is a knob or swelling, so something relating to such a swelling is lump-like.

clue.text: "Its the voice of the; I heard him declare" (Carroll)

definitions.text: "Its the voice of the; I heard him declare" (Carroll)

parts.words: "Its the voice of the; I heard him declare" (Carroll)
parts.note: a fill-in-the-blank quotation from the poem recited by Alice in Lewis Carroll's Wonderland, parodying Isaac Watts; the missing word is a shellfish

explanation.walkthrough: Lewis Carroll's verse, recited in the chapter with the quadrille, opens with this line; the gap takes the crustacean that the poem is about.
explanation.definitionFit: Carroll's parody replaces the sluggard of Watts's hymn with a large clawed sea crustacean.

clue.text: Make excessive demand on public with an old film?

parts.note: overt means open and public, not hidden
an gives A, the indefinite article
X was the old British certificate for an adults-only film

explanation.surface: Someone asking too much of the public by screening an old movie.
explanation.walkthrough: X was the former British cinema rating for adult films, before 18 replaced it.
explanation.definitionFit: To place too heavy a burden on someone is to strain them, like levying too great a duty.

clue.text: Some people put a brave face on it. Poles, perhaps?

definitions.text: Some people put a brave face on it. Poles, perhaps?

parts.words: Some people put a brave face on it. Poles, perhaps?
parts.note: a brave is a Native American warrior whose carved face might appear on it, and the Poles are not a nation but the carved wooden posts

explanation.walkthrough: 'brave face' sounds like stoicism and 'Poles' like people from Poland; both point to the carved emblem posts of North American peoples.
explanation.definitionFit: The carved emblem of a clan or tribe, often set up as a tall wooden pole bearing faces.

clue.text: Draughts reported in a country-house

indicators.note: reported signals that the word for the game is heard spoken, giving a different spelling

parts.note: draughts is the board game Americans call checkers

explanation.surface: News of a game of draughts at a stately home.
explanation.walkthrough: CHEQUERS, the British Prime Minister's official country residence in Buckinghamshire, sounds like CHECKERS, the American name for draughts.
explanation.definitionFit: The Prime Minister's official weekend retreat is a manor in the Buckinghamshire countryside.

clue.text: Arrant article on church opinion

parts.note: arrant means utter, complete
an is the indefinite article
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: Downright stuff written about the church's view.
explanation.definitionFit: An utterance is something said, a spoken view or statement.

clue.text: Copyright manager for a thriller-writer

parts.note: C is the copyright symbol
a handler manages someone, like a boxer's or agent's handler

explanation.surface: A rights manager working for a crime novelist.
explanation.walkthrough: Raymond Chandler wrote the Philip Marlowe detective novels.
explanation.definitionFit: Raymond Chandler was an American author of hard-boiled crime novels such as The Big Sleep.

clue.text: More than one cheat raises the wind in America

definitions.text: More than one cheat raises the wind in America

parts.words: More than one cheat raises the wind in America
parts.note: swindlers are dishonest people who get money by trickery, and in the US a tornado whirls up the air

explanation.walkthrough: 'Raise the wind' is a British idiom for getting money; cheats do that, while in America the same word names tornadoes, which literally raise wind.
explanation.definitionFit: Dishonest tricksters are crooks in British slang, and the word is also US slang for tornadoes.

clue.text: Gossip easy to pick up in St. Paul's?

definitions.text: easy to pick up in St. Paul's?

explanation.definitionFit: A rumour passed quietly around; and the dome of St Paul's Cathedral in London has a gallery where faint murmurs carry clearly across.

clue.text: Pot-companion in coach?

parts.note: a pot is what tea is brewed and served in, so a pot stands for the drink
CH stands for Companion of Honour, a British order

explanation.surface: A drinking partner sitting in a stagecoach.
explanation.walkthrough: CH is Companion of Honour, a British honour; 'in' is a link word, so 'coach' is a verb meaning instruct.
explanation.definitionFit: To coach a pupil is to tutor or instruct them.

clue.text: To eradicate boil, has treatment

indicators.note: treatment means working on or processing, so the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: Getting rid of a boil needs medical care.
explanation.walkthrough: 'treatment' fits medicine for a boil, but it rearranges BOILHAS.
explanation.definitionFit: To abolish is to do away with something entirely, to wipe it out.

clue.text: Italian barmaid left with first-class return

parts.note: port is the left side of a ship

indicators.note: return means to go back, so this pair of letters is turned round

parts.note: A1 means first-class, read here as the letters A and I

explanation.surface: An Italian pub server goes off with a top-quality reply.
explanation.walkthrough: 'barmaid' is a joke: Portia, in The Merchant of Venice, is a woman who pleads at the bar as a lawyer.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's heroine from Belmont disguises herself as a lawyer, appearing before the court's bar.

clue.text: This Japanese art is increasing, we are told

definitions.text: This Japanese art is increasing, we are told

parts.words: This Japanese art is increasing, we are told
parts.note: spoken aloud, 'is increasing' can be heard as 'is in creasing', a description of a Japanese craft of folded paper

explanation.walkthrough: 'increasing' looks like growth, but heard as 'in creasing' it describes paper folding.
explanation.definitionFit: The Japanese craft of folding paper into figures consists entirely of creases.

clue.text: Fabulous fellow to put forward a retirement

indicators.note: retirement means withdrawing, going backwards, so the letters are read in reverse

parts.note: to pose a question is to put it forward

explanation.surface: A man of legend proposes that someone retire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fabulous' does not mean wonderful but writing fables.
explanation.definitionFit: The ancient Greek storyteller is famous for his fables, so he is a fable-writing man.

clue.text: Marx operating weapon for attacking schools?

parts.note: Harpo was one of the Marx Brothers comedy team
something operating is on, switched on

explanation.surface: A Marx brother using a weapon to raid schools.
explanation.walkthrough: 'schools' are not classrooms but schools of whales or fish.
explanation.definitionFit: The barbed spear thrown at whales is a weapon used against groups of sea creatures.

clue.text: Table covering is apt to be embroidered

indicators.note: embroidered means worked over or embellished, so the letters of these two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A tablecloth that is suitable for needlework.
explanation.walkthrough: 'embroidered' fits a tablecloth, but here it rearranges ISAPT.
explanation.definitionFit: Tapis is an old word for a tapestry or cloth spread over a table.

clue.text: Old character assessment of warbler down under

parts.note: thorn is an Old English runic letter, written as a p with a tall stem
a bill is a statement of what is owed, an assessment of charges

explanation.surface: An old-fashioned report on a songbird in Australia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old character' suggests a person, but it is a letter of the Old English alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: Small Australian songbirds of this name are often called warblers.

clue.text: Advertise room in area available to fliers

parts.note: to air an idea is to make it public, to advertise it
room means space

explanation.surface: Advertising for vacant space in a district open to pilots.
explanation.definitionFit: The region of sky above a country, in which aircraft may fly.

clue.text: Bottom note, there transposed?

indicators.note: transposed means moved around, so the letters of this word are put in a different order

explanation.surface: A low musical note shifted to another key.
explanation.walkthrough: 'transposed' sounds musical, but rearranges THERE to ETHER.
explanation.definitionFit: Nether means lower, as in nether regions, so it is the lowest part.
